newsitem.title: USA: Clinton casts away crutches, walks with cane.
newsitem.headline: Clinton casts away crutches, walks with cane.

text.p: President Bill Clinton cast away his crutches on Monday and used a walking cane as he began the next phase of recovery from surgery on his right knee two months ago.
The president leaned on a single cane in his left hand when he walked from his limousine, shook hands with dignitaries and climbed the steps to board Air Force One at the end of a visit to Barbados.

White House spokeswoman Mary Ellen Glynn said earlier the president had conferred with his doctors and his physical therapist as well as first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton on Sunday at poolside to discuss his condition.
The president, wrapping up a week-long trip to Mexico, Costa Rica and Barbados, was due to arrive back in Washington later on Monday.

Clinton used one of a pair of carved, wooden canes given to him at the San Francisco monastery in Tlaxcala, Mexico, last week. He took a few steps with them when he received them and the canes had since been outfitted with rubber tips.
Clinton tore a tendon in his right knee during a stumble at the Florida estate of golfer Greg Norman in the early hours on March 14. He underwent surgery the same day to repair it.
The president has suffered back pain in recent days and Glynn said doctors believed the crutches might have been a cause.
During his weekend in Barbados, Clinton got into the swimming pool for some physical therapy at the Heron Bay estate where he stayed.
He set a grueling pace during the longest foreign trip he has taken since hurting the knee, but Glynn said one day of rest at poolside did much to rejuvenate him.
